question: A teacher wants Claude to answer student questions from a large and steadily growing set of course materials, across many separate chats. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Add the course materials to each chat; create a Project; ask questions in that project; keep the instructions brief.
B) Ask questions in a plain chat; keep the instructions brief; create a Project; add the course materials as project knowledge.
C) Keep the instructions brief; create a Project; ask questions in that project; add the course materials as project knowledge.
D) Create a Project; add the course materials as project knowledge; keep the instructions brief; ask questions in that project.
correct_answers: D) Create a Project; add the course materials as project knowledge; keep the instructions brief; ask questions in that project.
explanations: Incorrect. Pasting the materials into individual chats is the very repetition a project is meant to remove.
Incorrect. The questions are asked before any of the course materials exist as project knowledge, so those first answers have nothing to draw on.
Incorrect. Asking before the materials are uploaded means the early answers have nothing to draw on.
Correct. The project has to exist before materials can be attached, brief instructions leave more room for the materials themselves, and only chats started inside the project can draw on them.
